Rewrite your legacy applications piece-by-piece into Rust with behavior-checked automated migration paths and AI coding agent integration. 🦀✨

Tired of the massive risk and guesswork involved in all-or-nothing legacy rewrites? 

Meet rust-anything: a behavior-checked framework designed to systematically modernize heterogeneous codebases (TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, Ruby, C) into safe, high-performance Rust without risking regressions. 

Whether you are looking to squeeze a 20x speedup out of a slow Python parsing module or isolate a hot loop in a Node monolith, this tool lets you selectively adopt Rust exactly where you need it most.

Here is what makes it a game-changer for backend engineers and systems architects:

🔍 Behavior-Checked Replay Engine: Records thousands of real execution cases from your original application and enforces exact behavioral parity against your Rust port using record, diff, and gate workflows.

🌉 Multi-Language Bridge Generation: Automatically builds FFI and binding wrappers for TypeScript, Python, C, Go, Ruby, and Java using tools like NAPI-RS, PyO3, and WASM.

🤖 AI Coding Agent Integration: Features native Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and workflow skills that plug directly into Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI for automated profiling and porting assistance.

⚡ Performance Profiling: Pinpoints hot loops and bottlenecks, enabling zero-copy batch data transfers across language boundaries.

Stop risking production outages with manual migrations. Isolate your bottlenecks, guarantee functional equivalence, and future-proof your stack today.

👉 Check out the repository and drop a star:
https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything

Stop guessing your local LLM serving parameters and let science do the heavy lifting. 🚀

Most AI engineers waste countless hours tweaking random engine flags, never knowing if they have actually hit their hardware limits or are just staring at measurement noise. 

Meet inference-optimisation-skill: An agent skill designed to systematically hill-climb local LLM serving performance through theoretical ceiling calculations, rigorous A/B control interleaving, and long-context stability gates. 

Whether you are running vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, or ExLlama on consumer GPUs, Apple Silicon, or enterprise accelerators, this tool helps you squeeze maximum performance out of your hardware.

Key features you will love:
⚙️ Theoretical Ceiling Calculations: Computes exact memory bandwidth and FLOP limits before you even start tuning.
🔬 Rigorous A/B Testing Harness: Interleaved controls eliminate noise to measure true token metrics and residency.
🛡️ Comprehensive Validation Suite: Long-context needle retrieval gates, concurrent full-KV soaks, and memory watchdogs.
🛠️ Engine-Agnostic Tooling: Python and Bash scripts like bench.py and ceiling.py for OpenAI-compatible servers.

Say goodbye to arbitrary configuration tuning and hello to a repeatable, scientific optimization workflow. 

👉 Check out the repo and start optimizing: https://github.com/sybil-solutions/inference-optimisation-skill

Transform long-form videos and live streams into viral vertical clips automatically with this self-hosted, bring-your-own-key AI video pipeline. 🚀

Content repurposing is a massive time sink. Spending hours scrubbing through footage, transcribing audio, finding highlight moments, cropping to 9:16, adding captions, and posting to multiple platforms drains your energy and resources. 

Enter PeakCut (https://github.com/haziqahmedqasmi/PeakCut) - the open-source solution that automates the entire video clipping pipeline right from your own machine. 

Here is what makes it a game-changer for developers and media engineers:

🔒 Local Speech-to-Text: Utilizes sherpa-onnx and the Parakeet model so your audio data stays private and never leaves your machine.
⚡ Real-Time Live Streaming Clips: Features a rolling buffer that evaluates metrics like loudness, chat activity, and transcripts on the fly for live content.
🤖 BYOK Multi-Provider AI Engine: Seamlessly integrates with Gemini, OpenAI, Claude, Groq, Ollama, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
📱 Direct Auto-Posting: Built-in integrations for YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok complete with rate-limiting and daily caps.

Under the hood, it is built with a clean, modular Python codebase using FastAPI for the backend and zero-build HTML/CSS/JS for the frontend. It serves as the ultimate architectural blueprint for combining local audio transcription with LLM-based structured JSON extraction and social APIs without paying for expensive SaaS wrappers.

Ready to build your own private, cost-effective clipping automation? 

👉 Check out the repo and drop a star: https://github.com/haziqahmedqasmi/PeakCut

What if you could pack a complete offline survival library, local AI retrieval engine, and detailed state maps into a single zero-network desktop app? 🧳🤖🗺️

Engineers and developers are constantly challenged with packaging dense technical manuals, encyclopedias, video content, geospatial data, and functional AI retrieval into a fully offline-capable desktop bundle for Mac, Windows, and Linux. 

Enter Lastbook. It operates entirely air-gapped without listening ports or telemetry, using an in-memory bridge to connect native web views to a local Python backend. 

Here is what makes it a masterclass in offline-first engineering:
⚡ Zero-port in-memory desktop bridge connecting native GUI shells across platforms to a local Python engine without opening local sockets.
🧠 Air-gapped local AI runner and meaning-based search capable of answering questions and citing specific library pages without an internet connection.
🔒 Strict cryptographic supply-chain security featuring pinned Mozilla TLS roots, explicit HTTPS allow-lists, and automated package scans that fail builds on unauthorized network calls or test code.
📍 Granular offline map system providing vector-based state maps, terrain data, and local address searches without relying on remote geolocation services.

For systems engineers, security specialists, and AI developers, Lastbook is the ultimate blueprint for building zero-trust, air-gapped desktop applications. Study the architecture, explore the secure IPC bridges, and level up your local RAG pipelines.

Check out the source code and start building here:
https://github.com/Immortal-Protocols/lastbook

Tired of heavy vendor bloatware like Razer Synapse and Logitech G Hub eating up your RAM just to check a battery percentage? 🛑

We’ve all been there: installing massive, resource-heavy proprietary suites just to see if your wireless mouse or keyboard is about to die on your development workstation. 

Meet the ultimate lightweight alternative: Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor. ⚡

This standalone Windows tray utility queries your devices directly via HID and custom protocols, displaying real-time battery status straight onto your taskbar or system tray without the background tax. 

✨ Key Features:
• Ultra-lightweight footprint: A plain C++/Win32 app consuming roughly 350 KB on disk and a tiny 2 MB of RAM—zero runtimes or background services required.
• Direct communication: Bypasses heavy vendor suites entirely (though it can run alongside them without conflicts).
• Broad compatibility: Supports major brands including Logitech, Razer, SteelSeries, Corsair, HyperX, Pulsar, Keychron, Lamzu, VAXEE, and various console controllers.
• Native Windows integration: Features light/dark themes, DPI scaling, multi-monitor setups, and transparent taskbar support.

👨‍💻 For Developers:
Beyond being a killer productivity tool for minimalists and gamers, this repository is a masterclass in low-level Windows programming, pure C++/Win32 app design, and direct hardware interfacing. It’s an incredible reference implementation if you want to learn how to build high-performance desktop utilities that respect system resources and avoid heavy frameworks like Electron or .NET.

Check out the repo and clean up your system tray today:
https://github.com/krisgfx9/Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor
